name: QNB Group
founded: 1964 (incorporated in Qatar on 6 June 1964 under Amiri Decree No. 7 as the country's first Qatari-owned commercial bank)
ownership_summary: QSE-listed. Qatar Investment Authority (QIA) holds 50% of the ordinary shares; the remaining 50% is available to the public (FY2025 consolidated financial statements, note 22; official profile page, checked 12 Oct 2026). The FY2025 statements describe the Group as engaged in conventional and Islamic banking.
government_link: Yes - Qatar Investment Authority, Qatar's sovereign wealth fund, owns 50% of ordinary shares (FY2025 financial statements note 22; profile page checked 2026-10-12).
group_structure: Qatar National Bank (Q.P.S.C.) is the QSE-listed parent of QNB Group. Wealth-relevant subsidiaries: QNB (Suisse) SA (100%, Geneva private bank, FINMA-regulated, the Group's offshore private-banking hub), QNB Financial Services WLL (QNBFS, 100%, brokerage), QNB Capital LLC (100%, investment banking). Asset management is run as a division (Group Asset and Wealth Management), not a separate legal entity found in the subsidiary list. Largest foreign banking subsidiaries: QNB Bank A.S. (Türkiye, 99.88%), Enpara Bank A.S. (Türkiye digital bank, 99.88%), Qatar National Bank (S.A.E.) (Egypt, 95.0%), PT Bank QNB Indonesia (91.57%), QNB Tunisia, QNB Syria (50.8%), Mansour Bank (Iraq, 54.2%). Associates include Commercial Bank International (UAE, 40%; profiled separately as ae-cbi - equity-accounted, so do not add CBI balances to QNB totals), Housing Bank for Trade and Finance (Jordan, 38.6%), Ecobank Transnational (Togo, 20.1%) and Al Jazeera Finance (Qatar, 20%). The Group is establishing separate digital-bank entities (ezbank) in Saudi Arabia and Egypt. All figures in this file are Group consolidated unless stated.

footprint: Presence in more than 28 countries across three continents (profile page and H1 2026 release); 'nearly one thousand branches' and more than 5,390 ATMs including subsidiaries and associates, 31.5 thousand employees and 36 million customers (Annual Report 2025). International network page (checked 12 Oct 2026): Qatar, KSA, Kuwait, Oman, UAE (CBI associate), Egypt, Tunisia, Sudan, South Sudan, Togo (Ecobank), Iraq (Mansour Bank), Jordan (HBTF), Lebanon, Syria, Yemen, Türkiye, Switzerland, France, UK, India, Indonesia, Singapore, Hong Kong, plus representative offices in China and Vietnam. International Business contributed 53% of the business mix shown in the Annual Report 2025 'at a glance' page.
customer_segments: Retail (mass), affluent/premium (QNB First and QNB First Plus), private banking HNW/UHNW (QNB Private in Qatar; offshore via QNB (Suisse) SA; private banking in France and UK), SME/commercial, large corporate and institutional, financial institutions, sovereign/government; brokerage clients of QNBFS (retail, HNW, domestic and foreign institutions).
business_lines: Four reporting segments: Corporate Banking, Consumer Banking, Asset and Wealth Management, and International Banking (financial statements note 2). Annual Report 2025 business lines: Wholesale and Commercial Banking; Retail Banking (incl. QNB First / First Plus premium banking, cards, payments/acquiring, QNB Mobile); Asset and Wealth Management (private banking, in-house funds and discretionary mandates, open-architecture third-party funds, structured products, brokerage and custody via QNBFS, Swiss private bank QNB Suisse); International Business. Investment banking via QNB Capital. In H1 2026 the Asset and Wealth Management segment generated QR 687.4m revenue and held QR 50.5bn customer deposits and QR 44.7bn loans.

capabilities.wealth_summary: QNB runs wealth through a Group Asset and Wealth Management division (SEVP Abdulla Hashim Al-Sada) covering private banking, in-house asset management, open-architecture funds, structured products and brokerage; the division earned about QR 1.4bn revenue in 2025 and reports as its own segment (H1 2026: QR 687m revenue, QR 50.5bn deposits). Asset management AUM rose 12% to QR 29bn in 2025; it launched a QNB Money Market Fund and two thematic portfolios (AI/digital infrastructure and renewable energy/climate transition) and expanded reverse convertibles and multi-asset baskets. QNB Private (Qatar's first private bank, ~30% market share, Euromoney Best Private Bank in Qatar 2025) grew AUM ~50% in 2025, uses QNB (Suisse) SA in Geneva as its offshore hub, and is building a specialised wealth management system for client reporting. Affluent clients are served by QNB First (QAR 35k salary or QAR 350k balance) and First Plus. Third-party funds come via the Allfunds Bank platform (23-fund white list). Brokerage subsidiary QNBFS holds 46% of QSE trading, opened retail bond trading from QR 100,000 in Dec 2025, and is trialling an integrated multi-market retail trading platform for launch in 2026.

private_banking.detail: QNB Private in Qatar, which QNB calls the first private bank established in Qatar. It offers a dedicated private banker, banking, real estate services and advisory, asset and wealth management, Lombard/special lending, and access to QNB private banking in Switzerland, France and the UK. Offshore hub: QNB (Suisse) SA in Geneva (FINMA): open-architecture investing, equities and fixed income trading, structured products, QNB and third-party mutual and hedge funds, GCC and global brokerage and custody, Lombard and real-estate lending, Islamic solutions, UHNW concierge. 2025: AUM up ~50%, loans and deposits up ~7%, clients up 3%, ~30% Qatar market share; RMs got a new 360-degree client dashboard; a specialised wealth management system for client reporting is in development. Awards: Euromoney and MEED Best Private Bank in Qatar 2025; Global Finance Best Private Bank in the Middle East and Qatar 2025.

asset_management.detail: In-house division (Group Asset and Wealth Management; no separate asset-management legal entity found). AUM QR 29bn at end-2025 (+12%), revenue +7.7%; in-house funds averaged 330 bps net outperformance (S8). Funds: Al Watani Fund (Qatari blue chips), QNB MENA Debt Fund, QNB Sukuk Fund, QNB MENA Equity Fund, QNB Commodity Fund, and QNB Money Market Fund (launched 2025). QNB Suisse fund range: MENA Equities, MENA Debt, Global Sukuk, Spinel RC Fund, Global Funds ICAV. Two thematic portfolios launched in 2025 (AI/digital infrastructure; renewables/climate transition). Plans for cross-border fund structures and more automation and digital client tools in 2026.

brokerage.detail: QNB Financial Services WLL (QNBFS), wholly owned, brokerage since May 2011. QSE market share 46% in 2025 (33% 2023, 37% 2024); ~10% share of retail investors; 100% share of bonds and T-bill transactions; market maker and liquidity provider for 39 listed companies; only Qatari broker with equity research (30 companies). Markets: Qatar (web and mobile), GCC and Egypt (via desk), US/European equities, ETFs and primary issues (desk), global trading via Interactive Brokers, primary and secondary bonds and sukuk, margin trading. Retail bond trading on QSE from QR 100,000 launched Dec 2025. Retail clients are reached through QNB branches. CEO Maha Mohamad Al-Sulaiti.

digital_investing.detail: Through QNBFS rather than the bank app: the QNBFS Trading app (iOS/Android) and web trading for QSE, with transfers between QNB accounts and investment accounts. QNBFS is trialling a single integrated retail trading platform across Qatar, GCC, US and Europe with consolidated portfolio view, expected to launch in 2026, and is exploring AI-driven tailored recommendations (Annual Report 2025). No evidence found that the QNB Mobile banking app in Qatar sells funds or securities. Enpara (Türkiye) and the planned ezbank digital banks focus on banking, not investing, in the sources checked.

advisory.detail: End-to-end advisory by Group AWM (S8). The QNB Wealth Solutions team designs fund portfolios by region, asset class and manager (S12). Private bankers advise HNW clients, and QNB Suisse provides investment advisory (S16, S18).

discretionary.detail: Discretionary mandates are available: clients can assign portfolio management to QNB's Asset Management Division under agreed guidelines. Portfolio types include equities, commodities, Qatar/GCC/EM, fixed income and balanced, plus tailor-made or capital-guaranteed structures and ESG themes (Portfolio Management Services page). Aggregate performance of QNB's QE (Qatar equity) portfolios is published in the Annual Report.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No robo-advisor or digital model-portfolio service found. Closest offers: Wealth Solutions' custom fund portfolios (advisor-led), and the MetLife-underwritten International Wealth Builder savings plan with conservative, balanced or aggressive strategies.

funds_platform.detail: Third-party international funds are selected from the Allfunds Bank platform, then screened by the Asset Management Division and reviewed monthly; all must be UCITS and no-load. The monthly white list has 23 funds (20 third-party; 17 SFDR Art. 8). Managers include Goldman Sachs, Fidelity, Schroders, Allianz, BNP Paribas, Pictet, Amundi, Janus Henderson and Old Mutual. The open-architecture platform added aerospace and defence, healthcare and sustainable infrastructure funds in 2025.

structured_products.detail: Demand for structured solutions grew >15% in 2025, led by reverse convertibles; longer-term reverse convertibles and multi-asset baskets were added; private banking clients favour capital-protected and yield-enhancing notes (S8). QNB Suisse offers structured products (S18); QNB AWM offers capital-guaranteed structures (S14).

private_markets.detail: No private equity, private credit or other private-markets fund offering found. The Annual Report mentions investor appetite for 'alternative assets' and structured products giving diversified asset pools; the white list's 'alternatives' are a listed global property equity fund and a gold fund. QNB Suisse lists third-party hedge funds.

islamic_wealth.detail: QNB Sukuk Fund (USD sukuk from governments, agencies and corporates) and QNB Suisse Global Sukuk Fund; Old Mutual Global Islamic Equity fund on the white list; QNB Suisse Islamic solutions (Wakala, reverse Murabaha); QNBFS secondary sukuk trading. QNB Capital arranges sukuk (IFN Deal of the Year 2025 awards, Oct 2026).

initiatives.what: Asset management launched QNB Money Market Fund and two thematic portfolio solutions (AI/digital infrastructure; renewable energy/climate transition); expanded structured product range.
Private Banking introduced a 360-degree RM dashboard; a specialised wealth management system for client reporting is under development.
QNBFS launched retail trading of listed government and corporate bonds on QSE with a QR 100,000 minimum (previously up to QR 50m).
QNBFS trialling a single integrated retail trading platform (Qatar, GCC, US, Europe) with consolidated portfolio view; launch expected in 2026; exploring AI-driven recommendations.
Saudi digital banking licence for ezbank (JV with Ajlan & Bros, SAR 2.5bn); Egypt ezbank licence granted by CBE in Oct 2025 (approx. EGP 4.5bn); MVPs planned Dec 2026 (KSA) and Q1 2027 (Egypt).
QNBeyond Plus technology shared-services centre in Egypt operational, supporting digital-bank builds; QNB has onboarded ten local fintechs in Qatar.

opportunities: QNBFS is building a new integrated multi-market retail trading platform (expected 2026) and exploring AI-driven tailored investment recommendations (S8 p.71).
Private Banking has a specialised wealth management system for client reporting 'underway' and a new RM 360-degree dashboard (S8 p.70).
Asset management plans to 'improve efficiency and digitisation' through automation, data governance and client-focused digital tools in 2026, and to develop cross-border fund structures (S8 p.69).
No robo/model-portfolio or in-app fund investing found in the QNB Mobile app in Qatar; affluent QNB First base grew 6% in 2025 (S8 p.64).
No private-markets offering found despite stated client appetite for alternatives (S8 p.68).
barriers: Scale and in-house capability: QR 29bn in-house asset manager, own Swiss private bank (QNB Suisse) and market-leading broker (QNBFS 46% QSE share) (S8).
Existing third-party fund sourcing via Allfunds Bank and international execution via Interactive Brokers (S13, S19).
Group IT and digital builds are run in-house and via QNBeyond Plus (Egypt shared services) for new digital banks (S8).

discrepancies.detail: Enpara Bank's own site describes it as a subsidiary (istiraki) of Qatar National Bank (Q.P.S.C.) licensed by the BDDK in Aug 2024 (S36); Forbes Turkiye (1 Oct 2026) describes Enpara as having separated from QNB Bank A.S. a year earlier into independent-bank status (S37).
discrepancies.resolution: Both are consistent with Enpara being a direct QNB Group subsidiary rather than a unit of QNB Bank A.S.; the subsidiaries table (99.88% per FY2025 statements, S5) was not changed in the people pass - re-check ownership in the next metrics pass.
